abstract: Markman's secant-sheaf programme proves algebraicity of Weil classes on abelian 2n-folds once a sheaf on an abelian n-fold, with Chern character on a secant line of the spinor variety, is semiregular; it works for genus-three Jacobians. By Calabi–Yau adjunction, on abelian fourfolds the Buchweitz–Flenner map on Ext² is the transpose of Hochschild evaluation. This gives a Chern-character test: a simple fully semiregular sheaf satisfies χ(F,F)−2+2rk(c¹) ≤ rk(c²), with equality for line bundles and point ideals. For Markman's imaginary-quadratic secant characters χ = 8d²|c|²Θ⁴/4! > 0, so on every abelian fourfold, for every ample Θ, no simple sheaf with such a character is fully semiregular, and Perry's G-semiregularity for free translation groups does not rescue them. For the weaker condition his argument actually uses (injectivity on the image of evaluation), both his genus-four families also fail: they cannot deform to first order off the Jacobian locus. For theta-divisor sheaves, a non-Cartier surface does not survive smoothing the nodes of Θ; for union ideals, Brill–Noether loci are rigid (Lombardi–Tirabassi). By Künneth the failure lifts to his product objects on X×X̂, along a direction tangent to the Weil period domain. So Brill–Noether seeds work only in genus three. A variant covers his real-multiplication construction under a transversality hypothesis. A second, noncommutative obstruction holds on every principally polarized fourfold: a secant ideal sheaf with a reduced component of codimension at least three, or with two surface components meeting transversally, fails, and normalizing such meeting points does not help. This excludes Abel–Prym seeds and Markman's cyclic partial-normalization example (twist corrected to 3Θ). No new case of the Hodge conjecture is proved.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: v4 adds Corollaries G′ and G″ and implements the three minor notes of the v3 acceptance; no Hodge class changes status and no new general impossibility claim is made. (1) New Corollary G′ (with cm_symmetry_scout), after Theorem G: Markman's cyclic partial-normalization example [26, §12] (n = (d+9)/2 theta translates, m = (d+9)(2d−1) normalized nodes) has secant character (1,3,−d,−3d,d²) only with twist 3Θ, correcting the printed Θ; the (d+9)(d−2) remaining transverse nodes obstruct a bivector in ker c², by Theorem G(ii), so the example fails the weak criterion of [26, Question 11.4] for every odd d ≥ 3, also after descent by translations. New reference [26] = arXiv 2509.23403v2; new checker corollary_Gprime_check.py; one sentence in §7(d). (2) New Corollary G″ (audited by cm_symmetry_scout): at a partially normalized transverse double point, [O → O_P1 ⊕ O_P2], local Ext² = C² and constant bivectors obstruct by (−π12, π34), so normalizing nodes does not help; a fully normalized Z/15 carrier with character (1,10,−20,−200,400) is excluded; the local condition is stated precisely (local Ext² = 0 sufficient, not necessary). New checkers corollary_Gpp_check.py and normalized_point_ext.sing. (3) The summary of Theorem G(ii) in §1 now keeps 'at a point off the other components'. (4) §7(d) now states Corollary F′'s transversality hypothesis explicitly. (5) prym_seeds.py: the parameter formerly named ell is renamed eps and documented as the total correction ε = ℓ − δ of Remark 7.1; outputs unchanged in form.

coauthors.contribution: Theorem G: independent discovery of the local obstruction for point components, extension to curve components, audit of the proof, and the rank computation rk ob² = 18 vs rk c² = 12; audit of the relative-Orlov/Künneth step in Theorem F. Corollary G′ (v4): application of the transverse-plane obstruction to the remaining nodes of Markman's cyclic example, the proof text and its symbolic checker. Corollary G″ (v4): independent audit of the normalized-point obstruction (explicit cancellation of the unit summand, Ext² and obstruction vector), check of the fully normalized Z/15 example, and its checker; the precise form of the local condition.

title: A Chern-character test for semiregularity on abelian fourfolds, and the failure of Markman's imaginary-quadratic secant sheaves
